messages.subject: Cat bed advice
messages.text:
Hello! 

 We have eight rescued cats aged six months to 12 years. They seem quite happy with their assortment of beds but I wonder if the older ones in particular would benefit from your cat mats. Or if lining their existing beds with batting would be as effective while being less expensive.
 

 

 I'd really appreciate your advice.
 

 Thank you.
 

 Jeanine

messages.subject: Re: Cat bed advice
messages.text:
Hi Jeanine,

I'm sorry for the long silence on this, it's not how we like to do things, and I'll make it up by getting you a real answer now.

For older cats, the milkweed insulation does make a real difference. It's naturally hydrophobic (stays dry even if your cat drools or the mat gets damp), and because the hollow fibers trap air inside each strand rather than just between them, it holds warmth even under sustained pressure from a sleeping cat. A cat who runs cold or has joint stiffness tends to notice the difference.

As for lining their existing beds with batting: yes, that works, and it's the more economical path. Our insulation batting is available by the half-metre or metre at https://lasclay.com/en/products/isolant-asclepiade-vegan-naturel, you'd simply cut it to fit inside the bed cover. The performance is essentially the same as the finished cat mat; you're just doing the assembly yourself.

The dedicated cat cushions (https://lasclay.com/en/products/coussin-ecoresponsable-animaux) have a removable, washable cover and come in three sizes, which is convenient for a multi-cat household, but the batting route gets you the same warmth at lower cost per bed.

With eight cats, I'd suggest starting with a metre of batting and cutting a few test pieces for your oldest ones. If they claim the spots and stay there, you'll know it's worth doing the whole fleet.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
